newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Aborigines warn of jail "time bomb".
newsitem.headline: Australian Aborigines warn of jail "time bomb".

text.p: Australia's top Aboriginal body warned on Friday that the high imprisonment rate of young Aborigines was a potentially disastrous time bomb for the next century as deaths in custody continued at a high rate.
There have been five Aboriginal deaths in custody so far in 1997, compared with 18 in 1996 and 13 in 1995, according to a report by the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission (ATSIC).
The report released on Friday said the high rate of imprisonment for Aborigines remained a major factor in their above average death rate while in custody.
A report released in November found Aborigines were 1.26 times more likely to die in jail than white prisoners.

"It has been widely recognised that the high criminalisation and incarceration rates of indigenous young people is a disastrous time bomb, which will seriously affect the life chances of another generation of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people," the ATSIC report said.
The ATSIC report said that more than half the 475 inmates aged between 10 and 17 in juvenile detention centres at March 31, 1994, were indigenous Australians.
The report criticised national and state governments for failing to implement reforms aimed at reducing Aboriginal deaths in custody following an official inquiry in 1991.

Commission chairman Gatjil Djerrkura told journalists the latest report highlighted the need for governments to move quickly to improve the juvenile system through more appropriate penalties and alternatives to jail.
"There is still a great need for the resources to develop community-based strategies to divert young people from the justice system," Djerrkura said.
Aboriginal Affairs Minister John Herron said many of the problems leading to the high jail rate for young Aborigines began early in their lives.
"The cycle must be broken so that young people are given a chance to develop their skills and talents," Herron said.
Aborigines make up two percent of Australia's population of 18 million, but account for a disproportionately high number of those held in police custody and jail.
